title: 20-Year Treasury Bond auction (January second reopening) — the quieter of the two legs the 2027-01-14 announcement sizes, on a 24-of-24 reopening base rate
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-14 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised. Read verbatim from that text: `20-Year  BOND` carrying the legend marker `R` (`R --denotes reopening`), announced `Thursday, January 14, 2027`, auctioned `Wednesday, January 20, 2027`, settled `Friday, January 22, 2027`. The 1:00 p.m. ET bidding deadline is NOT taken from the schedule — it is sourced from fiscaldata `auctions_query`'s `closing_time_comp`, which reads `01:00 PM` on every 20-Year auction in the 2023-01-01 onward pull (n=44). Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-14 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09). PROPOSED BECAUSE IT IS ONE OF THE TWO COUPON LEGS THAT ANNOUNCEMENT EXISTS TO SIZE, and the calendar already tracks the other one (`treasury-10y-tips-2027-01-21`, which is in fact this announcement's proposer). Tracking one leg and not the other would leave the announcement's own outcome half-scoreable. WHAT IT IS, PRECISELY: the SECOND reopening (`19-Year 10-Month`) of the 20-Year new issue sold 2026-11-18, on the Feb/May/Aug/Nov new-issue rotation that has held four years. SIZE EXPECTATION for whoever researches it, with its base rate: $13B. Every 20-Year reopening since 2023-09-19 has printed $13B — 24 consecutive, zero deviations, against 13 consecutive new issues at $16B over the same span (fiscaldata `auctions_query`, security_type Bond, 2023-01-01 onward, n=44, pulled 2026-09-09). The January second-reopening slot specifically printed $13B in 2024-01-17, 2025-01-22 and 2026-01-21, 3 of 3. THE NUMBER IS NOT A GUESS AND WILL NOT BE ONE: Treasury's quarterly refunding statement publishes an anticipated-auction-size table whose 20-Year column names each month of the coming quarter, and the November refunding covers November through January — sb0305 (2025-11-05, read direct this session) published `Jan-26 ... 20-Year 13` and the 2026-01-21 auction printed $13B. So the 2026-11-04 refunding is where this auction's size becomes public, and `treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-14` is where it is read back. SESSION CONTEXT: this auction sits inside the MLK-shortened week (the PDF carries `Holiday - Monday, January 18, 2027 - Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.`), the day after all four of the announcement's bill legs auction on Tuesday 2027-01-19 and the day before the 10-Year TIPS new issue on Thursday 2027-01-21, with `vix-expiration-2027-01-20` the same morning and the FOMC communications blackout already running from 2027-01-16 into the 2027-01-27 meeting. Proposed as an estimate; `symbols: []` and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
